content:
Apple's annual September major launch event will be held this Wednesday, when three new iPhone models are expected to be unveiled: the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max and iPhone Ultra. Here's a preview.

iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max

The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max will succeed the widely popular iPhone 17 Pro series.

Rumoured features include:

  • A20 Pro chip with greater performance and improved efficiency
  • Major camera upgrades, including the addition of a variable aperture main lens
  • Dynamic Island reduced in size by 35%, giving the design a more modern look
  • New colour options, with a bold burgundy as the headline shade
  • Best battery life ever, with particularly notable gains on the iPhone 18 Pro Max
  • Redesigned Camera Control button
  • Apple's in-house C2 cellular modem
  • New satellite features, including 5G satellite connectivity

The expected starting price of the iPhone 18 Pro is also set to rise. Estimates put it at around US$1,399, but the writer believes actual pricing could be closer to US$1,199 or US$1,249.

iPhone Ultra

According to reports, the iPhone Ultra will be Apple's first foldable iPhone, with an expected price tag exceeding US$2,000, and will pioneer an entirely new premium product line.

The foldable design makes the iPhone Ultra Apple's most groundbreaking model to date. It will adopt a wide book-style folding form factor, with an outer display of around 5.4 inches and an inner display of 7.8 inches, similar in size to an iPad mini.

The design and materials are expected to follow the style of the iPhone Air, featuring a titanium frame with a clean, minimalist aesthetic.

The iPhone Ultra will come equipped with two rear cameras (main and ultra-wide) and two front cameras, one for each display. Authentication will use Touch ID instead of Face ID.

Software will be the standout feature of this device, running iOS 27, which supports side-by-side multitasking and adaptive landscape layouts, fully leveraging the new form factor.

Performance is expected to match the iPhone 18 Pro, with the same A20 Pro chip, along with a vapour chamber cooling system and the C2 modem.

Missing models: iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2

As usual, September typically sees the simultaneous launch of a new entry-level iPhone 18 and the successor to the iPhone Air.

However, reports suggest Apple will significantly revamp its autumn lineup this year, pushing back the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 to early 2027.

It remains unclear whether this arrangement is purely a strategic decision or a forced move dictated by the current memory shortage. Either way, with no more affordable models in the mix, this autumn's new iPhone lineup will be clearly focused on the high end.

Are you planning to upgrade to a new iPhone this autumn? Which model would you choose? Feel free to share in the comments section.
